files.html: //! examples/magic_isomorphic_keyboard - the computer keyboard as an instrument, its keys laid out so that every //! interval has one shape: the key to the right is a fifth up, the key below on the right a major third up, the key //! above on the right a minor third up (the drawn layout). Each row is the circle of fifths - F C G D A E B, //! then the sharps - so a major scale is seven keys in a row; a major chord is a downward triangle, its root, the key //! to its right and the key below between them, and a minor chord an upward one, its root, the key above on the right //! and the key to the right - in every key. It is the Tonnetz, the lattice of fifths and thirds, on a laptop's keys. //! //! ` 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0 - = a key's six neighbours: //! Q W E R T Y U I O P [ ] \ //! A S D F G H J K L ; ' up-left -4 up-right +3 //! Z X C V B N M , . / left -7 (key) right +7 //! down-left -3 down-right +4 //! //! The tonic sits on F, the home row's key under the left index finger, the one with the bump: in C major the home row //! from D to L is F C G D A E B, the tonic under the index finger and its fifth under the next. //! //! The first layout, the stickers' in the photo - a minor third down to the right, a major third up to the upper //! right - is kept as `thirds_layout`, for the layouts the options will offer. //! //! A key is named by its place, not by what it types (`z.KeyboardKey` is the physical key), so the layout is the same //! on QWERTY, AZERTY and Dvorak. A key sounds while it is held: its press arrives through `on_input` and starts its //! note at once, as in `audio_keyboard`, or is read each frame where the launcher does not call it. A key of the drawn //! keyboard sounds under a finger or the mouse, several fingers at once, each sliding from key to key. The notes are //! Shepard tones (`z.mixer.shepard_instrument`), as on the scale stars: each sounds its pitch class in every octave at //! once, so keys playing the same note an octave or more apart - F and I, both C in C major - sound the same note, and //! light up together. //! //! The keyboard's left side plays chords: the keys up to the column of 5, T, G and B whose note is one of the scale's //! play the scale's triad on that note - in C major a major chord on C, F and G, a minor one on D, E and A, the //! diminished one on B. One key, three notes: a laptop's keyboard often cannot report the three keys of a triangle held //! together (the plan's risk R1, measured). A chord starts note by note - root, third, fifth, a strum's delay apart - //! as on the two-handed star - and softly, at the chords' volume, so that what the right hand plays is heard over //! it. The left side's other keys, the sharps in C major, play their own note. //! //! ` 1 2 3 4 5 | the left side's chords in C major, the tonic on F: //! Q W E R T | //! A S D F G | ` C 1 G 2 Dm 3 Am 4 Em 5 B dim //! Z X C V B | Q B dim D F F C G G //! Z G X Dm C Am V Em B B dim //! //! The header holds the scale - its tonic's dropdown and its mode's, as the two-handed star's - and the chords' //! volume. The tonic stays on F whatever the scale: every key then plays its note in the new scale, and the left //! side's chords are the new scale's. //! //! The plan, its decisions and its stages: `src/notes/magic_isomorphic_keyboard_plan.md`. The Shepard instrument sounds /// a pitch class in every octave at once, so two keys an octave apart would sound alike - sent as one key, they sound /// once, held as long as either is. fn soundKeyOf(midi_key: u8) u8 { return 60 + midi_key % 12; } /// How strongly a key holds its notes: a chord's key softly - at the chords' volume (`State.chord_volume`), so that /// what the right hand plays is heard over the chord - any other key fully. const HoldLayer = enum { chord, full }; /// The most notes a key plays: a chord's three. const most_notes_of_key: usize = 3; /// What a key plays: the sound keys (`soundKeyOf`) of its notes, in the order they start - one for a note; a chord's /// root, third and fifth - and how strongly it holds them. const KeyNotes = struct { /// The sound keys: the first `count` are the key's notes. sound_keys: [most_notes_of_key]u8, count: usize, /// How strongly the notes are held: a chord's softly, a note's own key fully. layer: HoldLayer, /// One note, held fully. fn single(sound_key: u8) KeyNotes { return .{ .sound_keys = .{ sound_key, 0, 0 }, .count = 1, .layer = .full }; } /// The notes' sound keys, in the order they start. fn slice(notes: *const KeyNotes) []const u8 { return notes.sound_keys[0..notes.count]; } }; /// The chord the key at `key_index` plays under `layout` and `anchoring` in `scale`: a key of the keyboard's left side /// - up to the column of 5, T, G and B (`params.playing.last_chord_index_in_row`) - whose note is one of the scale's /// plays the scale's triad on that note: in C major a major chord on C, F and G, a minor one on D, E and A, the /// diminished one on B. Null for a key of the right side, for one whose note is outside the scale - a sharp, in C /// major - and for one whose note falls outside MIDI's range. fn chordOfKey( layout: Isomorphic, anchoring: Anchoring, scale: *const Scale, key_index: usize, ) ?ScaleChord { const is_on_chord_side: bool = playing_keys[key_index].index_in_row <= params.playing.last_chord_index_in_row; if (!is_on_chord_side) { return null; } const midi_key: u8 = midiKeyOf(layout, anchoring, scale.tonicPitchClass(), key_index) orelse return null; const pitch_class: u4 = @intCast(midi_key % 12); const degree: u8 = scale.degreeOfPitchClass(pitch_class) orelse return null; return scale.chordOf(degree); } /// What the key at `key_index` plays under `layout` and `anchoring` in `scale`: a chord's key (`chordOfKey`), the /// chord's three notes - root, third, fifth - held softly (`HoldLayer.chord`); any other key, its own note, held /// fully. const chord: ScaleChord = chordOfKey(layout, anchoring, scale, key_index) orelse return KeyNotes.single(soundKeyOf(midi_key)); var notes: KeyNotes = .{ .sound_keys = undefined, .count = most_notes_of_key, .layer = .chord }; for (&notes.sound_keys, chord.degrees()) |*sound_key, degree| { sound_key.* = soundKeyOf(scale.pitchClassOfDegree(degree)); } return notes; } /// The twelve notes' names as the stickers write them, by pitch class from C: sharps for the black keys. const sharp_note_names: [12][]const u8 = .{ "C", "C#", "D", "D#", "E", "F", "F#", "G", "G#", "A", "A#", "B" };
